summary.text: Robert C. Carroll is the Democratic and Working Families Party member of the Assembly for District 44, which covers Park Slope, Kensington, and Prospect Heights in Brooklyn, and won re-election on November 3, 2026.
A Brooklyn native and former election lawyer, he was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and chairs its Libraries and Education Technology Committee.
His official biography highlights his work on dyslexia and literacy, renewable energy, election law, and public transportation.

paragraphs.text: Carroll was born and raised in the 44th Assembly District and attended PS 230 in Kensington.
He struggled with dyslexia as a child, which he says shaped his legislative focus on literacy.
He graduated from SUNY Binghamton and holds a J.D. from New York Law School.

Before running for the Assembly he was an attorney and served as president of the Central Brooklyn Independent Democrats, a political club serving Park Slope and Windsor Terrace; a 2016 report said he was the club's youngest president, and in 2016 he described himself as a reformer.
Carroll was elected to the Assembly in 2016 to succeed Jim Brennan, who did not seek re-election.
He won the 2016 Democratic primary with about 90% of the vote and the general election with about 85%, also running on the Working Families Party line.

He chairs the Assembly Committee on Libraries and Education Technology and serves on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Election Law; Environmental Conservation; and Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committees.
His official biography says he has authored and passed 35 bills through the Legislature since being elected, 25 of which have been signed into law.

It names him as prime sponsor of the Build Public Renewables Act, included in the 2023-24 state budget, and as author of the Dyslexia Task Force Act and the Dyslexia Diagnosis Access Act (signed 2024).
Ballotpedia says his 2026 primaries were uncontested, so no primary vote was held.
According to the same biography, he lives in Park Slope with his wife Virginia and their two children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election over Glenn Nocera, according to unofficial results from the NYC Board of Elections.
